title: Is the chip sell-off spreading?
subtitle: One question, three engines
note: A real question from 25 November 2026, the day after chip shares gave back most of a one-day rally. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown. Companies are described, not named.

tries.label: The question, part by part
tries.source: Antevo Research, Executive Brief and Tremor Watch, 25 Nov 2026. Tremor Watch provisional: 697 of 753 pairs read.

items.name: Across markets
evidence: Tremor Watch Elevated, 2.42 times a normal week, week to 20 November; rank 288 of 1,351 Fridays since 2001
Down from High, 3.84 times, the week before
Realised volatility 1.59 times its normal

items.name: Where it sits
evidence: Taiwan and the US fear gauge: 5.12 standard deviations from their two-year norm, the most unusual pair of the week
Taiwan and the S&P 500: 4.55, moving closer than usual
On 24 November Taipei had risen 9.0% and Seoul 6.3% before the reversal

items.name: US shoppers and credit
evidence: Dow +0.9%, retailers +2.3% as the chip index fell 7.9% on 24 November
Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 from 91.9
US sectors broke 0.33 times as often as normal, credit 0.54

items.name: Metals
evidence: Gold −2.5%, silver −5.5%, copper −4.7% on 24 November while the dollar and the ten-year yield eased
Hong Kong shares and gold moved together 3.63 standard deviations above their norm
Commodity pairs broke 2.48 times as often as normal

items.name: The cause
evidence: A mid-November US rule requires licences for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil
Findings that could put tariffs on 16 economies were reported as imminent on 24 November

items.do: Watch for the US trade representative’s findings on 16 economies
items.why: Reported as imminent on 24 November; rates for allies may be 15% or below, steeper for China.

items.do: Read the mid-November US chip rule
items.why: Licences for advanced AI chips to five markets, and a 90-day window for data centres abroad serving Chinese customers.
If Taiwan’s pairs stay this unusual while the index eases, the strain is narrowing rather than spreading.
The US-China tariff truce and China’s pause on rare-earth export curbs both run out that day.

sections.title: Research, geopolitics desk
sections.so_what: The sell-off has a policy cause that is still unfolding: the next step is a publication date, not a market mood.
evidence: Mid-November US rule: licences for advanced AI chips to five markets; 90-day window for data centres abroad
Tariff findings on 16 economies reported as imminent on 24 November
The US-China truce and China’s rare-earth pause expire on 10 January 2027
Evidence thin on the tariff rates and on whether China retaliates before January

sections.title: Executive Brief
sections.verdict: The chip trade lost its repair
sections.so_what: Nothing about the cost of funding changed in a day; the tariff news did. The brief and the desk agree.
evidence: The chip index fell 7.9%; the largest AI chip designer 5.9%
The ten-year yield ended within a few basis points of where it began
Metals fell with chips, not with rates

sections.title: Tremor Watch
sections.so_what: The strain sits in markets tied to chips and metals, not in credit: on this reading it has not become a funding problem.
evidence: Volatility 2.63 times normal, commodities 2.48, bonds 2.12, equity regions 2.04
Currencies and crypto 0.15, US sectors 0.33, credit 0.54
Provisional: 697 of 753 pairs read; revised on Saturday

sections.title: Research, economy desk
sections.so_what: The safe-haven currencies are the one place the sell-off visibly spread this week; the Tremor reading is a week older.
evidence: A gauge of share-market fear rose above 30 on 24 November
The franc strengthened 1.5% against the dollar in the week to 25 November

links.text: The desk names the cause, a chip rule and tariff findings; the brief shows funding costs did not move. Both point to policy, not money, behind the fall.
Tremor sees US sectors calmer than usual; the brief sees money moving from chips into retailers. The rotation stayed inside US shares.
Taiwan is the most unusual market on the Tremor board, and the desk’s chip rule and tariff findings land hardest on chip makers there.
